quality_thesis: External base translation must visibly own the first lateral impulse. Feet ride the moving support before torso/guard catch up; inertial lag peels one trailing foot, a new catch re-establishes support, then base braking produces root overrun, counter-torque, late guard reopening, and a permanently displaced ready address.

novelty.force_owner: translating support base owns surge and brake; defender reacts through support rather than self-propelled translation
novelty.support_logic: both feet initially ride base; trailing pressure decays to forefoot, peels fully unsupported, sweeps above moving base, then catches a new base address before brake
novelty.contact_logic: zero threat contact; support-base contact topology is the causal channel
novelty.recovery_debt: base and root remain shifted left in world coordinates; guard width and stance remain slightly asymmetric

keys.name: MOVING_BASE_READY
keys.causal_role: establish a stable translating-base relationship before the external base owns force
keys.motion_arc_root_note: root stacked over still base; guard already asymmetric toward fixed world threat

keys.name: THREAT_READ_PRELOAD
keys.causal_role: pre-compress and orient guard before base acceleration
keys.motion_arc_root_note: knees and pelvis preload while base remains still; threat-facing hand rises before surge

keys.name: BASE_SURGE_ONSET
keys.causal_role: external base begins translating while body and guard lag in world space
keys.motion_arc_root_note: feet ride left with base first; pelvis follows less; head and guard lag against platform acceleration

keys.name: INERTIA_LAG_EXTREME
keys.causal_role: make inertial lag visible before support must reorganize
keys.motion_arc_root_note: base outruns pelvis left; torso counterleans right; right forefoot becomes the last trailing pressure point

keys.name: TRAILING_FOOT_PEEL
keys.causal_role: release the trailing foot because inertial demand exceeds its dwindling pressure authority
keys.motion_arc_root_note: left foot alone owns the accelerating base; right foot lifts visibly above surface instead of sliding as planted theater

keys.name: FREE_FOOT_SWEEP_REBASE
keys.causal_role: sweep the free foot to a new base address while guard resists being dragged off line
keys.motion_arc_root_note: single support carries root; free foot clears the moving surface and crosses inward; pelvis begins catching platform translation

keys.name: REAR_CATCH_ON_TRANSLATING_BASE
keys.causal_role: reacquire two-foot support on the moving base before the base brakes
keys.motion_arc_root_note: new right-foot catch compresses pelvis and shortens the world-facing guard line; catch is a causal join

keys.name: BASE_BRAKE_ROOT_OVERRUN
keys.causal_role: stop the base while pelvis and shoulders continue through their stored lateral momentum
keys.motion_arc_root_note: platform brake precedes root arrest; pelvis overruns left of the fresh support midpoint and guard trails

keys.name: COUNTER_TORQUE_RESTACK
keys.causal_role: reverse torso yaw over stable feet to pay the brake-induced overshoot
keys.motion_arc_root_note: feet stay fixed on stopped base while pelvis recenters right; shoulders counter-rotate later than hips

keys.name: LATE_GUARD_REOPEN
keys.causal_role: restore defensive width only after root and support have survived the moving-base brake
keys.motion_arc_root_note: root is nearly restacked but right hand remains late; base and feet do not return to their original world address

keys.name: DISPLACED_BASE_READY
keys.causal_role: finish ready at the translated world address with visible residual stance and guard debt
keys.motion_arc_root_note: platform, feet, and pelvis remain displaced left; final asymmetry proves recovery is not an idle reset
